To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal parameters of the optically pumped sub-millimeter laser depend strongly on the type of the active substance.
submillimeter laser output powers can be optimized by varying the pump power, the vapor pressure of the laser medium, the resonator length, and the diameter of the coupling hole.
the output power of optically pumped far-IR lasers can be increased by optimizing the design parameters of the lasers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of generating high-power submillimeter radiation in the range of 0.1 to 1 mm.
the development and investigation of the characteristics of submillimeter-wave lasers based on the optically pumped active media.
the development of the technology of optically pumped lasers operating in the 100-1000 μm wavelength range, which are based on the active substances HCOOH, C2H5I, CH3OH, and CH3I.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a high-pumping power, a large diameter of the pump radiation aperture, and a large diameter of a submillimeter laser output aperture, in the case where the resonator is of a stable type, is not the most efficient way to increase the output power of the laser, and it is not necessary to use a high vapor pressure of the working medium.
the results obtained can be used to design submillimeter lasers with a high output power and high efficiency.

, in the case of a submillimeter laser with the active medium of CH3OH, the optimum values of the pump power, the diameter of the coupling hole, and the length of the laser resonator are 0.5-1.5 W, 0.2-0.3 mm, and 0.2 m, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to achieve a 10-fold improvement of the output characteristics of optically pumped lasers.
the use of the HCOOCH2CH3 molecule as the active substance of optically pumped lasers in the submillimeter region is very promising.

the output power of optically pumped lasers is determined by the efficiency of pumping, by the rate of stimulated emission, and by the losses in the resonator, and the optimum conditions are achieved when the pumping and the stimulated emission rates are equal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high efficiency of the submillimeter laser can be attained by using a high vapor pressure of the working substance and a small coupling aperture.
the optimum vapor pressure of the working substance in the laser cavity depends on the resonator length and the diameter of the coupling hole.
the output power of optically pumped lasers can be increased significantly by increasing the diameter of the coupling window.
